analysts.summary: TipRanks: 28 Buy, 5 Hold, 2 Sell, average target $217.50. Initiations on Jul 7: Goldman $205, JPMorgan $225, BofA $235, Morgan Stanley $300 (all Buy), Raymond James Strong Buy $800, MoffettNathanson Neutral $131. RBC kept Buy $225 before Q3.

bear: ~$1.9T valuation leaves little room for execution misses.
Capex ~$20B a quarter; consensus sees debt rising toward ~$350B by 2029.
Lock-up releases of 1.3B+ shares now and ~798M in December vs a small float.
Starlink ARPU falling ($66 from $85) and subscriber adds missed in Q3.
Key-person and governance risk: Musk controls ~82% of votes.
bull: Q3 beat on every segment and first GAAP profit as a public company.
AI compute revenue nearly tripled q/q to $7.56B.
~$100B cash cushion after IPO and bond sale.
Unique launch and Starlink moat; spectrum deal could expand mobile.
Index inclusion path (Nasdaq-100 done; S&P 500 possible after four profitable quarters).

options.gexNote: Oct 26 strikes 125-170 sampled: call OI 8.5k vs put OI 3.4k. Net dealer gamma is positive above ~$142 and peaks at 150-155, which tends to pin price in the $145-155 zone; below the $142 flip, gamma turns negative and moves can accelerate toward the $140 put wall.

options.strategy: With IV near realised and lock-up supply ahead, there is no strong premium-selling edge; if wanting exposure, a cash-secured put near $130-135 (IPO price area) for Dec keeps entry below the gamma flip. Not an order, a framework.

politicians.summary: Six House members or spouses disclosed SPCX buys right after the June 12 IPO (247 Wall St, TIKR); no sales reported. None appear in the Unusual Whales congress history since 2026-10-17, and SPCX is not among the stocks most held by politicians.

financial.note: Cash and securities ~$93.5-100B at June 30 vs ~$36.8B debt and leases; Q3 GAAP profitable, but capex $19.6B in Q3 and ~$70B expected for 2026.

growth.note: Revenue +161% y/y in Q3 to $14.6B; AI segment $7.56B (from $2.56B in Q2); Starlink connectivity +69%.

moat.note: Dominant reusable launch, largest LEO broadband constellation (12M+ Starlink subscribers) and a large AI compute business; hard to replicate.

momentum.note: $147 vs $135 IPO price; well off the $225.64 high; 13-week range $104.83-176.42; rose ~4.6% after hours on Q3 beat.

valuation.note: ~$1.9T market cap is ~33x annualised Q3 revenue and ~43x a $45B 2026 revenue base case; no conventional peer is close.

summary: SpaceX (now including xAI and X) just posted its first operating profit as a public company: Q3 2026 revenue rose 161% to $14.6B, beating the $12.86B consensus, with $2.79B of operating income and $4.4B of net income ($0.35/share). At about $147 the market values it near $1.9T, roughly 33x annualised Q3 revenue, so almost all the value rests on the AI compute and Starlink growth path and on capex of about $20B a quarter paying off. Our $115-215 range (mid $160) brackets the price, so it is fairly valued with modest upside; heavy lock-up supply (1.3B shares eligible Oct 22, 328M more Oct 26 and ~798M Dec 8) argues against chasing. Neutral with low conviction.

valuation.method: (a) Peers: no true comparable; AI cloud peers trade at 2-14x forward sales and space peers at very high multiples on small bases. (b) Earnings power: if 2027 revenue reaches $80-100B (company says it is on target for a $100B run rate by end-2026) at a 20-30% operating margin, $16-30B of EBIT at 50-80x gives ~$0.8-2.4T EV, ~$65-185/share plus ~$5/share net cash. (c) Analyst targets: $131 (MoffettNathanson) to $800 (Raymond James), core range $205-300, TipRanks average $217.50. Fair range set at $115-215, mid $160, weighting (b) and the lower half of (c).
valuation.note: Trailing P/E not meaningful (only one profitable quarter). Peer multiples come from dated articles and could not be refreshed this run.
